Florida Property & Tax Scraper – Requirements

Version 1.1 · October 7, 2026

Given a property address and an owner name in Miami-Dade County, the scraper returns one JSON record combining Property Appraiser and Tax Collector data. Prior-year taxes are returned only when they are still delinquent. Worked example: 555 NE 15 ST UNIT 401, owner JUDE PATRICK JACOB, folio 01-3231-052-0010.

  1. Inputs and sources
  2. Search and matching workflow
  3. Property Appraiser fields
  4. Tax Collector: summary and delinquency
  5. Latest annual bill breakdown
  6. Validation rules and edge cases
  7. Standard JSON output

1. Inputs and sources

Inputs per order

InputExampleRequired
scrap_order_id10000001 (dummy)Yes
Property address (incl. unit)555 NE 15 ST UNIT 401Yes
Owner nameJUDE PATRICK JACOBYes
CountyMiami-DadeYes
transactionTypeREFI / PURCHASEYes (pass-through)

Sources (scraped in this order)

#SourceEntry pointWhat it gives
1Property Appraiser of Miami-Dade Countymiamidadepa.gov – Property Search (by address)Folio, property info, assessment, benefits, taxable values, legal description, sales
2Miami-Dade Tax Collectormdctaxcollector.gov – property tax search (by folio)Account summary, amount due, payment history, annual bill breakdown

The folio from source 1 is the join key for source 2. Search the Tax Collector by folio, never by address, to avoid picking up another unit in the same building.

2. Search and matching workflow

The scraper resolves address + owner to exactly one folio, then pulls everything else by that folio.

  1. Normalize the address. Uppercase; standardize suffixes and directionals (STREET→ST, NORTHEAST→NE); split out the unit from forms like UNIT 401, UNIT: 401, #401, APT 401 or a trailing 401.
  2. Search the Property Appraiser by address including unit. Condo buildings return many folios for one street address, so the unit is mandatory.
  3. Match the owner. Compare against every owner on the folio (comma-separated on the PA). Match if any one owner matches after removing punctuation and ignoring word order. Allow LLC/TRUST/ESTATE suffix differences.
  4. Decide the result.
    • One folio matches address + unit + owner → continue.
    • Address matches but owner does not → continue, set matchStatus = "OWNER_MISMATCH".
    • Several candidates, none matches the owner → stop, errorMessage = "Multiple parcels found, owner not matched", return candidate folios.
    • No result → stop, errorMessage = "Property not found".
  5. Scrape the Property Appraiser detail pages, including legal description and sales.
  6. Search the Tax Collector by folio; scrape Account Summary and Account History.
  7. Open the latest annual bill and scrape the full breakdown.
  8. Check every prior year for delinquency; keep only delinquent years in the output.

Benefits Information

Read every row and every year: Benefit, Type, one value per year. Blank cells → null. Example: Non-Homestead Cap / Assessment Reduction / 2026 null, 2025 null, 2024 $26,810. Capture the footnote too. Empty table → [].

Taxable Value Information

Four groups (County, School Board, City, Regional), each with Exemption Value and Taxable Value per year. Example 2026: exemptions $0, taxable $164,478.

4. Tax Collector: account summary and delinquency

The example account is paid in full with nothing due; the most recent payment was $3,007.15 on 11/25/2025.

Account Summary → TaxInformation

Output keyWhere on pageExample
accountNumberReal Estate Account #01-3231-052-0010
amountDueAmount Due panel ("paid in full" → $0.00)$0.00
statusMessageAmount Due panel, full sentenceYour account is paid in full. There is nothing due at this time.
lastPaymentDate"most recent payment was made on …"11/25/2025
lastPaymentAmountsame sentence$3,007.15
typederived: PAID / DUE / PARTIAL / DELINQUENT / UNKNOWNPAID

Account History → AccountHistory[]

Return only the current (latest) bill year. Paid prior years are read for the delinquency check but are not included in the output.

Delinquency → DelinquencyInformation

Florida real estate taxes become delinquent on April 1 of the year after the tax year. Check every Account History row; a prior year is returned in delinquentYears[] only if one of these rules is true:

CodeRule (return the year only if this is true)
PRIOR_YEAR_DUEAny year before the current bill year with amount due > $0
OPEN_CERTIFICATETax certificate present and not marked Redeemed
TAX_DEED_PENDINGTax deed application with no Sold / Redeemed / Cancelled outcome
CURRENT_YEAR_DUECurrent bill unpaid on or after April 1 of the following year

Each returned year carries billYear, billType, amountDue, status, code, any certificate / tax deed details, and the raw row text in note. hasActiveDelinquency = true when delinquentYears is not empty; totalPriorYearsDue = sum of their amounts due.

Not returned: years paid in full (even if paid late), redeemed certificates, completed tax deed sales, and years marked "Not Available" on the public site. For the example property all prior years are paid, so delinquentYears is empty.

Shape of a delinquent result (illustrative values, not this property):

{

    "totalPriorYearsDue": "$2,912.40",

5. Latest annual bill breakdown

The 2025 bill totals $3,132.45 at a combined millage of 20.37780, with no non-ad valorem assessments and no exemptions. Capture every line, not only the School Board group.

Bill header → BillDetails

taxYear (2025), folio, municipality (MIAMI), millCode (0101), paidBy (SHELLPOINT MORTGAGE SERVICES – escrow), receiptNumber, paidDate, paidAmount, mailingAddress, propertyAddress.

Non-ad valorem → NonAdValorem[]

levyingAuthority, footageUnits, rate, amount per row. Example is empty: return [] and NonAdValoremNote: "No Non-Ad Valorem assessments."

Exemptions → Exemptions{}

From the bill's EXEMPTIONS line and PA Taxable Value Information. Example has none: {} plus ExemptionsNote: "No exemptions". When present, key by name (e.g. HOMESTEAD: $25,000).

Amount if paid by → PaymentSchedule[]

Every date/amount pair (example: Nov 30, 2025 → $0.00). Miami-Dade gives a 4% early-payment discount in November down to 1% in February; $3,007.15 paid = $3,132.45 × 0.96. Store both totalTax and paidAmount so the difference is not read as an underpayment.

6. Validation rules and edge cases

  • Folio match: PA folio = Tax Collector account = bill folio.
  • Taxable value match: bill taxable value ($153,718) = PA prior-year (2025) taxable value; the bill lags the PA's latest roll year by one.
  • Line sum: sum of taxesLevied = adValorem (within $0.05). Example: $3,132.45.
  • Millage sum: line millages sum to millageRate. Example: 20.37780.
  • Total: adValorem + nonAdValorem = totalTax.
  • Zero land/building values on condos are valid, not missing data.
  • Blank cells → null; empty tables → []; never drop a key.
  • Missing sections: keep the key with an empty value plus a <Section>Note.
  • Multiple owners: always an array, in page order.
  • Timeouts: retry twice, then name the failing source in errorMessage and still return the other source's data.
